English name: Act on Inventions at Public Research Institutions
Original name(s): Lov om opfindelser ved offentlige forskningsinstitutioner (forskerpatentloven)
Description: The act regulates the management of intellectual property to inventions at public research institutions giving the institutions privilege to acquire ownership and negotiate IP-contracts with industry.
Objective(s): The overall purpose of the act is to ensure that research results generated by public funds are utilized for the Danish society through commercial exploitation.|Promote protection and facilitate transfer of intellectual property rights from public research to the private business sector.|Allow universities to invest in patenting, take equity in spinouts and provide an incentive structure, where commercial revenues are shared between institutions and the inventing researchers.
Background:
The act on inventions at public research institutions defines the ownership regime for intellectual property at universities, university hospitals and government research institutes.

The progress in performance since 2000 has been monitored in annual commercialization surveys and addressed in a number of evaluations. In 2019 a national expert group finalized a review of the legal framework and institutional practice for technology transfer, which subsequently also informed the 2019 International Peer Review of the Danish Research & Innovation System (Horizon 2020 Policy Support Facility)

English name: Tri-Agency Open Access Policy on Publications
Description: The policy stipulates that grant recipients are required to ensure that any peer-reviewed journal publications arising from Agency-supported research are freely accessible within 12 months of publication.
Objective(s): The objective of this policy is to improve access to the results of Agency-funded research, and to increase the dissemination and exchange of research results. All researchers, regardless of funding support, are encouraged to adhere to this policy.
Background:
Momentum for open access has been growing as numerous funding agencies and institutions worldwide implement open access policies. The Canadas federal granting agencies strongly support open access to research results which promotes the principle of knowledge sharing and mobilization – an essential objective of academia. As research and scholarship become increasingly multi-disciplinary and collaborative, both domestically and internationally, the Agencies are working to facilitate research partnerships by harmonizing domestic policies and aligning with the global movement to open access.

In July 2023, the Presidents of the Agencies announced the review of the OA Policy, with the goal of requiring that any peer-reviewed journal publications arising from agency-supported research be freely available, without subscription or fee, at the time of publication. In February 2025, the agencies invited feedback on the draft revised policy. The renewed OA Policy will be released by the end of 2025.

Description: Born from Knowledge (BfK) is a programme promoted by the National Innovation Agency (ANI) and designed to support multiple levels of the Academic Spin-off cycle, from the initial ideation, to capacity-building for entrepreneurs and recognition of successful cases with prizes.
Objective(s): Raise awareness about the importance of investment in Science, Research, and Development (R&D) and its economic impact.|Operate in relevant areas and functions, offering a complete and integrated set of supports (financial and capacity-building).|Promote, disseminate, and reward good practices and success stories, including previously generated knowledge.|Increase the percentage of scientific and technological knowledge applied in innovation, contributing to the transformation of the business sector and generating economic and social impact.|Generate and promote scientific and technological employment, both in existing companies and organizations and through the creation of new knowledge-based companies.|Foster a culture and practices of Open Science and Open Innovation.
Background:
This initiative was created to:
1) promote an entrepreneurial attitude in Academia, disseminating good practices and creating a visible path for entrepreneurs at all Higher Education organizations in Portugal;
2) support concrete projects and entrepreneurs, through capacity-building and prizes.

In the current environment, with all participating Academic institutions having created internal mechanisms to support entrepreneurial initiatives, the programme is entering a new phase, with a bigger focus on deep tech spin-offs, which shall be supported through vouchers for diverse services (Deep2Start Programme).


BfK initiatives include:
- an idea contest (BfK Ideas) to rewards business ideas from students and researchers from Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) that result from R&D activities or the scientific and/or technological knowledge of their promoters;

- an Acceleration Program (BfK Rise) aimed at enhancing the value of the results of Research & Development (R&D) and existing technologies within the National Scientific and Technological System (SCTN) with commercialization potential;

- a distinction (BfK Awards) to recognize projects and companies “born from knowledge” that stand out in Research & Development (R&D) activities, particularly collaborative ones.

Description: Imec.istart is imec’s Business Accelerator Program.
Objective(s): Support tech start-ups with coaching, facilities and funding.
Background:
The imec.istart business acceleration program offers an initial investment of at least €50,000 to €250,000 (in exchange for shares), personal coaching and mentoring, a broad investor and partner network, free office space for one year and numerous other financial benefits to (future) tech entrepreneurs. Imec.istart creates a safe environment for the start-up in which they take into account and provide answers to the risks associated with the start-up of a new company.

In 2020 a capital increase was performed imec.istart fund nv. The Flemish Government decided in 2020 to invest 1,728,000 euro in the fund. This capital increase should make it possible to carry out investments in new start-ups up to and including 2027. From 2028, according to the business plan, imec.istart fund should be self-supporting, i.e. the funds that flow back to the fund from the sale of existing participations through exits should be sufficient to new investments and operating costs. Imec.istart fund will be transformed into an evergreen structure.

Description:
The Hellenic Industrial Property Organization (OBI) launched in 1995 the Regional Patent Libraries network, currently named as Regional Sub-offices. The initial network included 3 Libraries that were relaunched in 2018 and since 2019 has been expanded to 4 more cities, thus providing services in 6 regions: Macedonia (Thessaloniki and Kozani), Peloponnese (Patras), Crete (Heraklion), Central Greece (Volos), Epirus (Ioannina) and Thrace (Xanthi and Komotini).

The Regional Sub-offices provide:
– technological information from Patents at National and International level
– information and personalized assistance on industrial property protection and research results
– information to the public
– transfer and diffusion of technological information to any interested party in Greece
– printed information related to the Organisation and its services, as well as application forms for protection titles
– help and guidelines to the applicants on the filling of applications for protection titles (Patents, Utility Models, Designs, Trademarks). The available information at this level is enough to get knowledge of the level of the prior art at a first stage and to apply for “pre-research”.

Original name(s): Στρατηγική Εξυπνης Εξειδίκευσης για την Κύπρο για την περίοδο 2023-2030
Description: The Smart Specialisation Strategy (S3) for Cyprus for the period 2023-2030 was adopted by the Council of Ministers on 30 March 2023. It replaces the first Smart Specialisation Strategy "S3CY" that was developed in 2015 and covered the period until 2022.
Objective(s):
To support R&I in the priority sectors and their focus areas, as identified by S3|General Objective 1:
Diversify the economy to be more sustainable and resilient, rely less on natural resources and take advantage of green and digital technologies

Specific Objective 1:
Diversify to new technological fields of high knowledge complexity by relying on related technological and business capabilities

Specific Objective 2:
Diversify existing competencies to enter into new niches of relatively low complexity|General Objective 2:
Citizens enjoy happy, healthy and safe life with good rewarding jobs

Specific Objective 3:
Address health and environmental challenges
Background:
The S3 is based on a study conducted by the Technopolis group. The study builds on the analysis of the interim evaluation of the national R&I Programme "RESTART 2016-2020" and the participation of Cyprus in Horizon 2020 and on comprehensive desk research, taking into consideration European and national policies and priorities as highlighted by the long-term strategy "Vision 2035", the reforms and investments under the RRP etc.
The priorities of S3 are organised around 4 groups:
1) Technological priority areas - include digital technologies and innovative materials
2) Ecosystems - include Agrifood, Renewable Energy and Maritime and Shipping
3) Emerging ecosystems - include Space
4) Enablers - include Health and the Environment

The S3 will be incorporated to the new National R&I Strategy 2030, under preparation by the DMRID (to be adopted by the Council of Ministers in the next few months). Specifically, under Pillar D "Sectorial Priorities". The Action Plan of the National Strategy will include measures, actions and initiatives with emphasis to funding programmes for each Pillar/Priority, including for the implementation of S3.

As regards monitoring and evaluation, this will be decided once the National Strategy and its Action Plan are adopted. The DMRID will be responsible for the management of the National Strategy and the new S3.

English name: Technology Agency of the Czech Republic - Competitive Research Funds
Description: The Technology Agency of the Czech Republic (hereinafter referred to as “TA CR”), provider of competitive funding for applied research and innovation, was founded in 2009 by the Act No. 130/2002 Coll. on the support of research, experimental development and innovation.
Objective(s): Strengthen public-private partnerships in research, development and innovation.|Promote research, development and innovation for the needs of the government, especially public administration bodies.|Foster the commercialisation of public research.|Support applied research and experimental development.|Support the establishment and operation of centres of research, development and innovation in advanced fields.
Background:
The creation of TA CR was one of the cornerstones of the fundamental reforms in RDI in the Czech Republic as it simplifies the state support of applied research and experimental development which has been fragmented and implemented by many bodies before the reform. While in the past, the support of applied research and development used to be dispersed among large number of providers, today it is mainly concentrated in TA CR. The support of applied research through a single institution allows easier following of long-term aims and also to connect institutions with similar focus. TA CR also collaborates with other public administration bodies and with similar agencies - both domestic and foreign.

In the period 2019-2020 the mandate of TA CR did not changed. All their programmes are still in progress (each programme is briefly described below), with continuously widening their activities in launching and administrating new programs.

Following programmes under TA CR administration deal with joint programing and thus contribute to RDI policy in different institutions.

The BETA2 programme is a new follow-up programme approved in 2016 to continue the BETA programme and is aimed at promoting research, development and innovation for the needs of the government, especially public administration bodies that are not providers of support for RDI. The objectives of the programme are to enhance current practices, methodologies, regulatory mechanisms, supervision activities, and to improve services, information and products and processes that will lead to greater innovation, efficiency and effective allocation of public funds.

The GAMMA 2 programme supports the verification and validation of research results created in the research performing organizations. The programme is divided into two subprogrammes: The 1st sub-programme helps to verify if the result of research performed by the research organization is applicable in the practice. The 2nd sub-programme offers support to enterprises that are trying to bring innovative products to the market whose development was supported with the use of public funding and is prepared as a continuation of European framework programme SME instrument Phase 1 discontinued in the Horizon Europe.

The DELTA 2 programme supports the collaboration in applied research and experimental development of Czech enterprises and research organizations with their foreign partners. Only joint projects with partners from countries where TA CR has partner institution can apply. Main aim of the programme is to enable Czech enterprises and research organizations to cooperate with foreign partners (for example from Canada, China, Brazil, Israel, South Korea, Taiwan or Vietnam).

The KAPPA programme supports international cooperation between Czech entities and partners from Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein while interconnecting research organisations within the application sphere.
TA CR is also active in so called ERA-NET Cofund scheme of Hirozon 2020.

The EPSILON programme is mainly focused on improving the standing of the Czech Republic, as well as European industry in a global context, through the support of applied research and experimental development, whose results have a high potential for rapid application in new products, production processes and services.

The ZETA programme aims to support upcoming generation of researchers up to 35 years of age. It focuses on support collaboration between research organizations and enterprises. The programme is also orientated towards supporting women in research work. Under this programme will be possible to support international projects in frame of ERA NET Cofound or Marie Sklodowska Curie Actions.

The ETA programme aims to strengthen social and human dimensions in activities of applied research, experimental development and innovation and apply the outputs of these activities in the form of new or substantially improved existing products, procedures, processes or services.

The THETA programme aims to contribute in the medium and long term to fulfilling the vision of transformation and modernization of the energy sector in accordance with the approved strategic materials through the outputs, results and impacts of the supported projects. This aim will be achieved by supporting research, development and innovation in the energy sector.

The NATIONAL COMPETENCE CENTRE programme supports the establishment and operation of centres of research, development and innovation in advanced fields. The resulting centres create conditions for the development of long-term cooperation in research, development and innovation between the public and private sectors. Therefore, only consortia consisting of research organizations and enterprises, which are required to co-finance projects from private sources, are eligible to participate in the programme.
In 2019, TA CR expanded its programme portfolio by taking control over departmental programmes for the Ministry of Industry and Trade (TREND programme; the programme consist of support both to technology leaders and companies which are new to R&D&I public funding), the Ministry of the Environment (Evironment for Life programme) and the Ministry of Transport (TRANSPORT 2020+ programme). The provider of implementation of all three departmental programmes is TA CR. The implementation of the above mentioned programmes in the Agency‘s system will allow the applicants and subsidy beneficiaries in various programmes to apply for support in the same manner, under the same conditions, and in the same place.

TACR is a member of the Taftie European network of innovation agencies which gives us the opportunity to share experience and information with partner
agencies that also support research, development and innovations in various parts of the world.

Through activities focused on gender equality, we at the Technology Agency of the Czech Republic strive to remove barriers that restrict the assertion of human talent and abilities in the field of research, development and innovation. At the same time, our goal is to support research projects that – in addition to economic or environmental impacts – also ask themselves questions about their social relevance. We strive to ensure that publicly funded research and innovation also address the issues of diversity, inclusion or social justice of research impacts, thus having a positive impact on society as a whole – men, women or other groups. Through our activities in these areas, we join leading European agencies and participate in harmonizing the conditions for providing support in the European Research Area. TA CR was also a first funding provider from EU 13 to introduce a criterion for evaluating the gender dimension in research content in order to ensure equal benefits of applied research and innovation for women and men.

TA CR also has its own TA CR Award that is being awarded yearly. The award goes to most succesfuly completed projects in five categories - Business, Governance, Partnership, Society, and MIT-Country for the Future Award. The Awards are to highlight sucesful Czech ideas and research enceavours.

Description: The SAYEM Green Transformation Call is one of several initiatives launched by TÜBİTAK as part of the six-year Türkiye Green Industry Project. This call, led by the private sector in collaboration with universities and public institutions, promotes the establishment of specialised R&D and Innovation Platforms. Background: The SAYEM funding mechanism allows private sector firms, especially those with R&D and product design centres, to form networks with other firms in the value chain of targeted technology-based products, including end-users, technology development zones, public research institutes, and universities. This collaboration enhances the working cultures of the private sector, universities, and public research institutes, increasing their national and international competitiveness. The SAYEM Green Transformation Call, launched in 2023, aims to support Productization Programs to establish specialised R&D and Innovation Platforms led by the private sector. These platforms will create Productization Roadmaps to develop products or product groups for green transformation, utilising public resources for effective R&D support. Activities are expected to begin at the TRL 5-6 level, analysing the social, ecological, cultural, and economic impacts to generate tangible benefits for society.

Description: Under the leadership of the Health Institutes of Turkey (TÜSEB), the National Health Technology Initiative represents a transformative step towards enhancing Türkiye’s domestic capabilities in healthcare innovation and medical technology development. Description: The State Plan for Scientific and Technological Research and Innovation (PEICTI) is a multi-year planning instrument designed to establish the objectives, priorities, and programmes of research and innovation policies to be developed by the State Administration. Promote regional and local cooperation by leveraging territorial synergies. Support priority intervention areas. Promote framework conditions including compliance with open science principles; promote equality and diversity; ensure real and effective equality between men and women and diversity in all areas of SECTI; promote administrative simplification and reduce bureaucracy; and promote eco-responsibility to contribute to the ecological transition.
Background: The PEICTI 2024-2027 is developed in the context of recent legislative reforms, including the modification of the Science Law and the approval of the LOSU and the Startups Law. It aims to consolidate advances made during the previous plan (PEICTI 2021-2023) and align with national and European strategies impacting research and innovation policies. The programmes are structured in a matrix with two dimensions: five vertical programmes (Human Resources; Research and Experimental Development; Transfer and Collaboration; Innovation; R&D&I Infrastructures) and three cross-cutting programmes (Internationalisation; Regional Collaboration; Strategic Lines). This structure facilitates the complementarity of actions and the overall vision of the PEICTI. Framework conditions identified as essential across all programmes include commitment to the Open Science Policy, promotion of equality and diversity, administrative simplification and reduction of bureaucracy, and eco-responsibility.

It aims to enhance the "third mission" of universities by fostering an entrepreneurial culture and improving knowledge transfer capacities, including intellectual property management. Activities include assessing R&D product potential through patent and market analyses, protecting intellectual property, marketing R&D products, accrediting new laboratories or methods, conducting proof-of-concept activities, providing open access to R&D services, and creating demonstration and simulation spaces for presenting R&D products. Original name(s): Programului naţional în domeniile cercetării şi inovării pentru anii 2024-2027
Description: The National Programme in the Fields of Research and Innovation for 2024–2027 establishes the main priorities for public research funding in Moldova. It focuses on enhancing research excellence, promoting innovation, strengthening the connection between research and the economy, and supporting participation in European research and innovation initiatives. The programme aims to create a more competitive and internationally integrated research environment.
Objective(s): Integration into the European Research Area (ERA).|Increase investment in research and innovation.|Reform research funding mechanisms.|Strengthen academia–industry collaboration.|Attract and retain researchers, especially young talent.|Boost participation in international research programmes.
Background:
The National Programme in the Fields of Research and Innovation for 2024–2027 was developed amid Moldova's growing commitment to modernise its research and innovation system and align more closely with EU and international standards. This shift is driven by Moldova's ambition to strengthen its knowledge economy, enhance competitiveness, and address key societal challenges such as climate change, digitalisation, and public health. The programme responds to long-standing issues in the national research and innovation ecosystem, including underfunding, weak research infrastructure, limited international collaboration, and the outflow of skilled researchers.

Over the past two years, Moldova has made notable changes in its policy approach. The new programme introduces a more strategic, performance-oriented funding system, replacing fragmented or institutionally static models. It includes institutional reforms, such as the establishment of the Advisory Council for Science and Technology, and introduces competitive funding calls aligned with national and EU priorities. Emphasis is placed on young researcher engagement, public–private partnerships, and integration into European research and innovation frameworks, particularly Horizon Europe. These shifts signal a transition from reactive and short-term planning to a coherent, impact-driven research and innovation policy framework that aims to enhance both the scientific base and the country's innovation capacity.

Description: The Roadmap on Innovation and Technology Transfer for the Republic of Moldova is a strategic framework designed to strengthen the country's innovation ecosystem. Background:
The Roadmap on Innovation and Technology Transfer for the Republic of Moldova was developed by the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) in collaboration with the Ministry of Education and Research and finalised in early 2023. It emerged from the Innovation for Sustainable Development Review of Moldova (I4SDR), which identified key areas for enhancing the country's innovation ecosystem.

Over the past two years, Moldova has undertaken significant policy shifts to bolster its innovation and technology transfer landscape. These include the approval of the Smart Moldova National Programme (2024–2027), focusing on smart specialisation in sectors such as agriculture, ICT, energy, and biomedicine to foster innovation-driven economic growth and enhance human resource capacities. The Moldova Innovation Technology Park (MITP) operational period was extended from 10 to 20 years with a maintained 7% single tax rate until 2035, demonstrating government commitment to supporting technology businesses and startups. Additionally, the Digital Transformation Strategy (2023–2030) was approved to develop a digital society, strengthen the ICT sector, and create an innovative digital economy aligned with Moldova's European integration goals.

Description: This is a specialised national legal framework that provides intellectual property protection for plant varieties by granting exclusive rights to qualified plant breeders. Description: NETVAL was founded in November 2002 as a network of universities and public research organizations in Italy. It then became an association in September 2007, now has more than 70 members representing over 80% of the Italian public research system. Several IRCCS (research hospitals) have also recently joined NETVAL.
Objective(s):
NETVAL’s mission includes:
• sharing and strengthening the skills of Italian Universities and Public Research Organizations
in the field of the valorisation of research results;
• providing an interface with industry;
• consolidating expertise in the area of commercial projects and intellectual property management;
• developing international contacts for the benefit of NETVAL’s members.
Background: Netval was born in response to the so-called "Tremonti standard", known as "inventions to inventors" (art. 7, law 383/2001), which had actually introduced a disparity between researchers employed in the public and private sectors, AND between public researchers themselves , but above all it had made the relationship between companies and the world of public research extremely difficult. Since its introduction it had been heavily criticized by the university world, the business world and by researchers themselves.

Description: National priorities of oriented research, experimental development and innovation is a set of new RDI priorities closely linked to the social, economic and environmental needs of the sustainable development of the Czech Republic.
Objective(s): The priorities are of a forward looking nature, anticipating the most significant possible future threats and challenges in the following six areas: 1. Competitive knowledge-based economy, 2. Sustainability of energetics and material resources, 3. Environment for quality life, 4. Social and cultural challenges, 5. Healthy population, 6. Safe society.

One of the goals is to review the current priorities of the applied RDI. The RDI Priorities will be subsequently used in the preparation of the RDI programs to provide targeted support as well as institutional support for the development of research organizations. The RDI Priorities will be also used in drafting the state budget expenditures on RDI.

English name: Intellectual Property Academy and Industrial Property Rights Training Centre
Original name(s): Fikri Mülkiyet Akademisi ve Sınai Mülkiyet Hakları Eğitim Merkezi
Description:
The IP Academy provides in-house training for trademark and patent examiners, as well as assistant trademark and patent examiners. It also offers distance learning programs in cooperation with WIPO and training programs for high school students.

The academy operates through two training centers: the “Copyright Training Center,” under the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, and the “Industrial Property Training Center,” under the Turkish Patent and Trademark Office.
Objective(s): To support the intellectual property education among the IP professionals, examiners, attorneys and users|To increase the IP knowledge and awareness among the public|To provide educational material on IPR through every available tool that will facilitate more people (including practitioners -judges, examiners, lawyers etc.)|To increase implementation and enforcement of rights to a desired level
Background:
In order to conduct training, consultancy, and research activities related to intellectual property rights, the Intellectual Property Academy was established. Additionally, to carry out training activities related to industrial property rights within the structure of the Office, the Industrial Property Rights Training Centre was created. The working procedures and rules of the Intellectual Property Academy and the training centers, including secretariat services, fees for services provided, training activities, and other matters, will be determined by a regulation jointly administered by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism and the Office.

Industrial property education is among the most important priorities of TURKPATENT. To enhance education in this field, TURKPATENT has made every effort within its capacity. The Training Centre was initially designed to offer courses to TURKPATENT’s examiners on substantive matters. Over time, the variety of courses and the range of beneficiaries have expanded through cooperation with WIPO and other international organizations. The courses now include a broader range of stakeholders, such as patent and trademark attorneys, TTOs, right holders, and others, covering more comprehensive topics in intellectual property.

In the medium to long term, the scope of the Training Centre is planned to be further expanded. By providing educational materials on IPR through all available tools, the aim is to enable more people—including practitioners such as judges, examiners, and lawyers—to benefit. This, in turn, is expected to improve the implementation and enforcement of intellectual property rights to the desired level.

An online platform was launched in 2025 to further facilitate access to educational resources.

The Industrial Property Law No. 6769, Article 122, provides insights on "Inventions Generated in Projects Supported by the State." Framework provisions are introduced within the Industrial Property Law No. 6769 regarding the ownership of patent rights generated through projects supported by governmental institutions/bodies, with the aim of incentivizing inventions in these projects. These framework provisions also focus on promoting broad participation in R&D studies and encouraging cooperation between governmental institutions/bodies and commercial firms.

Article 122, which provides details on Inventions Generated in Projects Supported by the State, is outlined below:

ARTICLE 122: It shall be obligatory to notify the supporting institution of inventions generated in projects supported by State institutions and organizations, in compliance with the regulation. The party who benefitted from the project support shall, within one year from the date of the notification, inform the public institution in writing of their decision on whether they will claim ownership rights to the invention. If the beneficiary party of the project support does not claim ownership rights, or if they fail to notify their decision in writing, the supporting State institution or organization may take over the ownership rights to the invention. The beneficiary party of the project support cannot make statements or take actions that affect the invention’s eligibility for obtaining a patent or utility model status until the process regarding ownership rights is finalized.
If the beneficiary party of the project support claims ownership rights to the invention, they shall be obliged to file a patent application for the invention. The supporting State institution or organization shall be specified in the application.
The State institution or organization has the right to request regular updates from the beneficiary party of the project support regarding the use of the invention that is the subject of the patent, or regarding the efforts made to commercialize it. The commercial and financial information requested by the State institution or organization shall be kept confidential. The method of sharing the revenue earned from the use of the invention shall be determined by an agreement.

Original name(s): Закон за авторското право и сродните му права
Description: adopted in 1993 and amended in 2002, the law distinguishes 10 intellectual property types.
Objective(s): to protect scientific intellectual property|to protect results of research and development activities
Background:
The copyright in collections, anthologies, bibliographic works, databases and other similar material shall belong to the person who has collected or arranged the works and/or material contained therein unless otherwise agreed in a contract. The copyright in the individual parts of which such a work may consist and which themselves constitute works of literature, art and science shall belong to the individual authors thereof. Unless provided otherwise by law, works and parts of works thereof may not be included in collections without the consent of their authors. For inventors - they are subject to patenting according to the Law on patents and utility model registration, after which they receive protection for a term of 20 years from the date of priority (in case of payment of the annual maintenance fees). For utility models - They are subject to registration according to the Law on patents and utility model registration, after which they receive protection for a term of 4 years, with 2 possible extensions of 3 years.For industrial designs - They are subject to registration according to the Law on industrial designs, after which they receive protection for a term of 10 years, with 3 possible extensions of 5 years. For plant varietes - they are subject to registration according to the Law on the protection of new plant varieties and animal breeds, after which they receive protection for a term of 25 years from the date of certificate issuance (30 years for the vine and tree varieties.For animals breeds - they are subject to registration according to the Law on the protection of new plant varieties and animal breeds, after which they receive protection for a term of 30 years from the date of certificate issuance. For topographies of integrated circuits - they are subject to registration according to the Law on topography of integrated circuits, after which they receive protection for a term of 10 years from the date of the first commercial use (if application for registration is filed in term of 2 years afterwards) or from the date of the application for registration (if no commercial use has started or it has only been secretly realized). For scientific works - they are subject to copyright protection according to the Law on copyright and neighbouring rights, starting automatically with the work creation for the duration of the author’s life and 70 years after author’s death. For computer programs- they are subject to copyright protection according to the Law on copyright and neighbouring rights, starting automatically, with a duration of 70 years from making the program publicly available (for programs, created under employment) or for the life of the author and 70 years after his death (if the program is not created under employment). Moreover, there are special regulations about the ownership and rights on computer programs, different from the rest of works. For data bases - they are subject to dual protection according to the Law on copyright and neighbouring rights – through copyright as works on one hand, and through the so called sui generis rights – for a term of 15 years from the data base creation or from its making publicly available, if made available.
For other types - Literary and artistic works (subject to copyright protection according to the Law on copyright and neighbouring rights); Performances, phonograms, recordings of audio-visual works, radio and television programs (subject to neighbouring rights protection according to the Law on copyright and neighbouring rights); Trademarks and geographical indications (subject to protection according to the Law on marks and geographical indications); Trade names (subject to protection according to the Law in the commerce); Trade secrets (subject to protection according to the Law on the protection of competition). For competent bodies - the Patent Office– for inventions, utility models, industrial designs, trademarks, geographical indications, plant varieties, animal breeds, integrated circuits topographies; the Ministry of culture – for scientific, literary and artistic works, performances, phonograms, recordings of audio-visual works, radio and television programs, data bases; the Commission for protection of competition – for the protection against unfair competition.

Background:
The Digital Transformation Office (DTO) is developing the National Open Data Portal to make data available to the public as open government data. The National Open Data Portal, which will be implemented as part of the Open Data Project, is a data-sharing platform that will present anonymized and secure open government data to citizens and scientists through a common open data portal, as well as create value from the data in this context.

In this context, efforts are underway regarding the Open Data Project and the open government data portal (https://veri.gov.tr) carried out by the DTO. The technical aspect of this initiative is the software infrastructure, which has been completed. Specifically, the software infrastructure of “veri.gov.tr,” the national open government data portal, has been finalized, and a portal compliant with international standards has been designed. “Veri.gov.tr” was built using the CKAN open-source software in line with good practice examples. Additionally, the metadata configurations of the data to be presented on the portal have been designed in accordance with the international DCAT 2.0 metadata standard, ensuring compatibility for harvesting, which is a sustainable method.

The data to be published on the portal were collected from institutions, and anonymization and data cleaning processes were carried out before transferring the data to the test environment. Efforts are ongoing to transfer data from institutions suitable for harvesting to the portal. The portal is expected to be launched following the completion of the relevant legislative processes.

In addition to preparing the technical infrastructure for open government data sharing, the "Open Government Data Circular Draft" was prepared and presented to institutions as part of the legal and legislative infrastructure efforts. Within this framework, the aim is to establish data management procedures, legal and administrative regulatory infrastructures, and guidance documents for open government data as part of the open government data legislation efforts.

Furthermore, current situation analysis studies on the subject have been conducted, and research is ongoing to develop the National Open Data Portal in compliance with international standards. In this context, DTO coordinates a number of technical, legal, and organizational processes for the dissemination of public data as open government data. Efforts to establish data management methods, legal and administrative regulatory infrastructures, and guidance documents for open government data are also ongoing.

The Open Data Project aims to support uninterrupted artificial intelligence studies that rely on data and to enable the development of innovative technologies in Türkiye, generating value from data in economic and social fields. Within the scope of the project, the goal is to present public data in an open government data format in compliance with privacy principles, while adhering to the principles of transparency, openness, and accountability in public administration.

Description:
National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (NAIS) is the first national strategy document of our country on artificial intelligence (AI), which is relesaed publicly on 22 August 2021.
NAIS was prepared in accordance with the 11th Development Plan and Presidential Annual Programs, as well as the "Digital Türkiye" vision and the "National Technology Initiative".
Objective(s): To train AI Experts and Increasing Employment in the Domain.|To support Research, Entrepreneurship and Innovation.|To facilitate Access to Quality Data and Technical Infrastructure.|To regulate to Accelerate Socioeconomic Adaptation.|To strengthen International Cooperation.|To accelerate Structural and Labor Transformation.
Background:
The Presidential Circular No. 2021/18 on the "National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2021-2025", prepared in cooperation with the Digital Transformation Office of the Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye and the Ministry of Industry and Technology, and with active participation of all relevant stakeholders, entered into force upon its publication in the Official Gazette dated 20/08/2021 and numbered 31574.

The Strategy was prepared with a participatory approach. A comprehensive work was carried out with the contributions of many stakeholders such as public institutions, academia, professional organizations, private sector, NGOs and international organizations.

Having the vision "creating value on a global scale with an agile and sustainable AI ecosystem for a prosperous Türkiye", the Strategy was designed around 6 strategic priorities.

1. Training AI Experts and Increasing Employment in the Domain
2. Supporting Research, Entrepreneurship and Innovation
3. Facilitating Access to Quality Data and Technical Infrastructure
4. Regulating to Accelerate Socioeconomic Adaptation
5. Strengthening International Cooperation
6. Accelerating Structural and Labor Transformation

Within the scope of these strategic priorities, 24 objectives and 119 measures were determined.
NAIS sets the measures that will align our country's efforts on AI for the period 2021-2025.

Implementation process of the Strategy is coordinated by the "NAIS Steering Committee", chaired by the Vice President. The governance mechanism embraces “AI Ecosystem Advisory Group” and working groups where all relevant stakeholders are represented including NGOs, academia and private sector. In this context, this governance mechanism developed the action plan in detail towards guidance, reference models and standards; infrastructures and platforms and data resources.
The "AI Ecosystem Advisory Group" ensures the active contribution of the NGOs that takes place in the steering mechanism and to make a preliminary assessment to determine the NGOs to be included in the Advisory Group. To date, the participation of 11 AI and informatics related NGOs are provided. The current field-specific works of NGOs on AI and their possible contributions to the implementation process of the strategy are determined:
• Current studies in AI
• Their roadmap and planned activities in the field of AI
• Possible national and international contributions to the implementation process of NAIS and experts and areas of expertise that can be involved in the working groups

Besides, 7 working groups have been established to work in a cross-cutting manner:
• Human Resources WG
• Data Governance WG
• AI Law and Ethics WG
• Technical Infrastructure and Platforms WG
• Reliable and Responsible Artificial Intelligence WG
• Public Artificial Intelligence Ecosystem WG
• Sectoral Co-development Laboratories WG
The Working Group's primary responsibilities include supporting the NAIS Action Plan process, offering support for actions, and introducing innovations to the agenda. Member distribution of the working groups is as follows: Public sector (59%); University (22%); Private sector (12%); NGOs (%7).
At the 2nd NAIS Steering Committee on April 21, 2022, the working groups and the coordinating institutions responsible for the execution of the working groups were determined, and the activity processes of the Working Groups were initiated.
The Working Group's primary responsibilities include supporting the NAIS Action Plan process, offering support for actions, and introducing innovations to the agenda.
Some of the activities that have and are being carried out within the scope of the action plan are listed below:
• Artificial Intelligence Profession Mapping Workshop was held and Artificial Intelligence Occupation Map was created. In this context, sub-fields of Artificial Intelligence and Data Management & Processing were determined and job definition studies were carried out.
• Among the candidates who applied to the National Internship Program, more than 3000 students who received training on AI and participated in various activities were identified during the evaluation phase and included in the AI Young Talent Pool created on the Career Gate Platform (https://kariyerkapisi.cbiko.gov.tr ). The AI Young Talent Pool was opened to employers and in 2022, more than 2700 internship offers were sent by employers to students in this talent pool.
• AI Ecosystem Call is launched. Applications for projects were accepted between February 11, 2022, and May 23, 2022 (at 23:59), and the call's review procedures were finished. The call's findings were posted and made public on the TUBITAK website on August 23, 2202. Out of 22 project applications, 10 projects had an approval percentage of 45.5%, while 12 were turned down. The accepted projects under to be supported have a total budget of 12,665,448 TL.
• A current situation analysis has been made for thematic clusters and centers of excellence in the field of artificial intelligence. Center of Excellence, Cluster and Centers of Excellence & Support for Cluster Formation and Incentives & Thematic Formations on Artificial Intelligence in Türkiye.
• In order to develop advanced digital technologies in fields such as data science, AI, robotics, cyber security and intelligent autonomous systems in our country, and to strengthen cooperation between academia, public and industry in these technology fields; The Digital Innovation Collaboration Platform was launched by the Digital Transformation Office (DTO) on December 20, 2022 with the support of the Ministry of Industry and Technology and the Ministry of Youth and Sports
• An inventory template was created by determining High Performance Computing infrastructure criteria and an inventory was created by collecting High Performance Computing data from stakeholders such as Public Institutions/Private Sector/University over this template.
• “Central Public Data Space” project is launched to enable data-oriented innovation and transformation by encouraging secure data sharing in public institutions of Türkiye.
• Preparation studies towards an “AI Risk Framework” is started as part of the NAIS, which is intended to develop a trustworthy AI Audit Mechanism. Through the creation of the NAIS Risk Management Framework, it is intended to suggest methods to decrease risks associated with AI and to align the development process with normative criteria.
• In collaboration with the public sector, NGOs hosted a number of artificial intelligence events as well as an aviation, technology, and space technology festival (TeknoFest).
• Active participation is ensured in AI spesific events organized by/within: Digital Europe Programme (DEP), GPAI, OECD CDEP – WPAIGO, UNESCO, G20, CoE, NATO, CEN, CENELEC, IEC.
• AI Co-development Laboratories are established under TÜBİTAK BİLGEM YZE (AI Institute).
• For public AI initiatives and required areas, an inventory has been produced. The AI and Advanced Analytics Maturity Model and Project Management Handbook are still in the early stages of baseline research.
• Public AI Ecosystem Project Call under «KAMAG 1007» support program will be launched in 2023 in collaboration with Digital Transformation Office (DTO) and TÜBİTAK. The Public Institutions Research and Development Projects Support Program (1007 Program) is in effect in order to meet the needs of public institutions that can be met through R&D or to address their problems.

The Public Institutions Research and Development Projects Support Program (1007 Program) is in effect in order to meet the needs of public institutions that can be met through R&D or to address their problems.

Some of the activities that have and are being carried out within the scope of the action plan are listed below:
• Artificial Intelligence Profession Mapping Workshop was held and Artificial Intelligence Occupation Map was created. In this context, sub-fields of Artificial Intelligence and Data Management & Processing were determined and job definition studies were carried out.
• Among the candidates who applied to the National Internship Program, more than 3000 students who received training on AI and participated in various activities were identified during the evaluation phase and included in the AI Young Talent Pool created on the Career Gate Platform (https://kariyerkapisi.cbiko.gov.tr ). The AI Young Talent Pool was opened to employers and in 2022, more than 2700 internship offers were sent by employers to students in this talent pool.
• AI Ecosystem Call is launched. Applications for projects were accepted between February 11, 2022, and May 23, 2022 (at 23:59), and the call's review procedures were finished. The call's findings were posted and made public on the TUBITAK website on August 23, 2202. Out of 22 project applications, 10 projects had an approval percentage of 45.5%, while 12 were turned down. The accepted projects under to be supported have a total budget of 12,665,448 TL.
• A current situation analysis has been made for thematic clusters and centers of excellence in the field of artificial intelligence. Center of Excellence, Cluster and Centers of Excellence & Support for Cluster Formation and Incentives & Thematic Formations on Artificial Intelligence in Türkiye.
• In order to develop advanced digital technologies in fields such as data science, AI, robotics, cyber security and intelligent autonomous systems in our country, and to strengthen cooperation between academia, public and industry in these technology fields; The Digital Innovation Collaboration Platform was launched by the Digital Transformation Office (DTO) on December 20, 2022 with the support of the Ministry of Industry and Technology and the Ministry of Youth and Sports
• An inventory template was created by determining High Performance Computing infrastructure criteria and an inventory was created by collecting High Performance Computing data from stakeholders such as Public Institutions/Private Sector/University over this template.
• “Central Public Data Space” project is launched to enable data-oriented innovation and transformation by encouraging secure data sharing in public institutions of Türkiye.
• Preparation studies towards an “AI Risk Framework” is started as part of the NAIS, which is intended to develop a trustworthy AI Audit Mechanism. Through the creation of the NAIS Risk Management Framework, it is intended to suggest methods to decrease risks associated with AI and to align the development process with normative criteria.
• In collaboration with the public sector, NGOs hosted a number of artificial intelligence events as well as an aviation, technology, and space technology festival (TeknoFest).
• Active participation is ensured in AI spesific events organized by/within: Digital Europe Programme (DEP), GPAI, OECD CDEP – WPAIGO, UNESCO, G20, CoE, NATO, CEN, CENELEC, IEC.
• AI Co-development Laboratories are established under TÜBİTAK BİLGEM YZE (AI Institute).
• For public AI initiatives and required areas, an inventory has been produced. The AI and Advanced Analytics Maturity Model and Project Management Handbook are still in the early stages of baseline research.
• Public AI Ecosystem Project Call under «KAMAG 1007» support program will be launched in 2023 in collaboration with Digital Transformation Office (DTO) and TÜBİTAK. The Public Institutions Research and Development Projects Support Program (1007 Program) is in effect in order to meet the needs of public institutions that can be met through R&D or to address their problems.

Taking into account the recent developments in the field of AI and the 12th Development Plan, the Action Plan has been updated as the 2024-2025 Action Plan.

English name: Civic Coding - Innovation Network AI for the Common Good
Original name(s): Civic Coding - Innovationsnetz KI für das Gemeinwohl
Description: In order to promote social innovations and, in particular, the use of AI by society for the common good, even across ministry boundaries, Civic Coding bundles and linkes the AI-related projects, programs and structures of the three involved ministries in an open network that aims at the common good-oriented use of AI technologies.
Objective(s): Broaden the approach of the Future Fund to spread the social use of AI for the common good.|Promote AI skills on a broad basis and to take up social impulses for the social and sustainable design of AI technology.
Background:
The Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (BMAS), the Federal Ministry for Family Affairs, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth (BMFSFJ) and the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation, Nuclear Safety and Consumer Protection (BMUV) have joined together to develop "Civic Coding" - an innovation network AI for the common good. The aim is to establish a visible and effective innovation network that supports and secures the development and use of AI for the common good to strengthen our society, our environment and our social interaction in the long term.

To this end, the ministries contribute three infrastructure projects (so-called “anchor projects”) developed by them and implemented within their areas of responsibility into Civic Coding which are opened up and linked for joint use: the Civic Innovation Platform of the BMAS, that connects and promotes stakeholders from a wide range of sectors and industries who want to jointly use AI applications for the common good; the Civic Data Lab of the BMFSFJ, that supports civil society in collecting, utilising and sharing data; and the ECO AI LAB of the BMUV, which is a contact point for anyone who wants to use digital tools, data analyses and artificial intelligence for environmental protection. Since 2025, the Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV) has joined the initiative as a new cooperation partner.

Civic Coding was presented to the public for the first time in May 2021. An office has been established in January 2023 to support the Civic Coding initiative as well as to implement activities and support measures to promote the social use of AI for the common good. The various cross-ministerial support activities include, among other things, the Civic Coding project advisory service: It provided a low-threshold support service for project managers of AI technologies for the common good. The support service gave them easy access to the expertise of experts in technical, organisational, legal or formal issues. Up to 100 projects were supported over the course of the programme. A total of 113 projects applied in the period from April to September 2024. 87 project teams made use of the advisory service from May to October 2024. Information on the various activities and formats of the initiative as well as insights into the supported projects can be found here: https://www.civic-coding.de/

Description: This law establishes the legal, economic, organisational, and financial principles for state regulation of technology transfer activities in Ukraine. It aims to ensure the effective utilisation of the country's scientific, technical, and intellectual potential, protect property rights related to domestic technologies and their components, and promote international scientific and technical cooperation in this field.

Description: The Strategy for the Development of the Innovative Activity Sphere up to 2030 was approved by the Government of Ukraine by order of the Cabinet of Ministers on 10 July 2019 (No. 526-r). It supports innovation infrastructure and structures involved in knowledge transfer, including science and technology parks, clusters, technology platforms, centres of expertise and technology transfer, and startup incubators such as accelerators and business incubators.

Background: Until 2019, Ukraine lacked a national-level strategic document on innovation development. Following an analysis of state policy in innovation activity, this Strategy was developed and adopted. It is implemented through approved action plans every three years. The Strategy focuses on creating a favourable regulatory framework for innovative business entities; developing innovation infrastructure, methodological and consulting support; expanding connections between domestic scientists and foreign enterprises; and increasing capacity through cultural and educational activities to foster innovative culture and support career development for young graduates.

Description: Latvian Smart Specialisation Strategy (RIS3) is a strategy for the transformation of the economy towards higher added value, productivity and more efficient use of resources. Currently, the economy of Latvias challenge is to ensure the development of the sectors of future growth, where products and services with a high added value exist or could appear.
Objective(s): To change the current structure of production and export in traditional fields of economy.|to support knowledge-and technology-driven growth and catching up on the development of knowledge-based skills.|To develop Latvian science, technology and innovation into a system that is competitive on a global scale and capable of satisfying the development needs of the economy and society.|To develop future areas of growth where new goods and services can be created with a high added value.|To develop fields with a horizontal impact on the transformation of the economy.
Background:
The task of RIS3 is to ensure the prioritisation of development and regular review of development priorities, targeting of public investment, including the selection of policy instruments corresponding to the strategic settings, and development of a monitoring system that allows tracking the influence of public investments and ensures maximum progress towards the achievement of established goals. According to the Guidelines for the Development of Science, Technology and Innovation 2014–2020, RIS3 prescribes finding constant competitive advantages, choosing strategic priorities and selection of such policy instruments that unleashes the maximum potential of national knowledge-based development, and thus ensures economic growth. RIS3 provides three directions of the transformation of economy: 1) the change of production and export structure in the traditional sectors of the economy; 2) development of the sectors of future growth, where products and services with a high added value exist or could appear; 3) development of the sectors with a significant horizontal impact and contribution to the transformation of economy. Such choice of directions is based on the share of the traditional sectors in the economy, research excellence in a number of high added value related industries, as well as the need to ensure sustainable use of the limited resources of Latvia.

English name: TUBITAK 1513 Technology Transfer Offices Grant Program
Original name(s): TÜBİTAK 1513 Teknoloji Transfer Ofisleri Destekleme Programı
Description: The TÜBİTAK 1513 Technology Transfer Office Support Program aims to support technology transfer offices that operate in order to contribute to the commercialization of information and technologies produced in universities and technology development regions and thus to create economic, social and cultural value.
Objective(s): To promote technology transfer interface structures that facilitate university-industry cooperation and the utilization of academic knowledge and new technologies through the commercialization of academic research results.|To promote the utilization of national and international support mechanisms by public and private universities.|To promote academic entrepreneurship by enhancing the effectiveness of technology transfer offices as interface mechanisms.|To contribute to the commercialization of knowledge and technologies developed in universities and technology development regions, thereby generating economic, social, and cultural value.
Background:
TÜBİTAK implemented a science and technology policy tool related to Technology Transfer Offices (TTOs) and initiated the 1513 Technology Transfer Offices Program in 2012 to enhance academic research capacity in universities and encourage technology transfer activities. The program aims to increase university-industry collaborations, IP management, licensing, commercialization, and the establishment of spin-off/start-up companies.

While the institutional capacities of universities in the field of technology transfer have been improved through the support provided under the 1513 and 1601 Programs, TÜBİTAK-TEYDEB has gained competence in effectively supporting interface mechanisms. In May 2018, the Principles of the Technology Transfer Offices Support Program were updated in line with legislation on intellectual property rights and the organizational structure of technology transfer offices. A performance-oriented support process was designed to encourage the transformation of knowledge in universities into economic value.

Under the updated support mechanism, technology transfer offices that institutionalize their business processes and develop revenue models are expected to effectively protect inventions in higher education institutions and manage their intellectual property portfolios. In this context, transferring inventions from higher education institutions to industry or commercializing them through incorporation and generating revenue from these activities are key performance indicators for technology transfer offices.

The program consists of two phases: Institutional Capacity Building and Target-Oriented Growth.

The maximum duration of support in both phases is 5 years, allowing a technology transfer office to benefit from the program for up to 10 years. Support rates are 80% for the first 5 years and 60% for the second 5 years. The budget cap for the Institutional Capacity Building Phase is 1,250,000 TL per year, while the cap for the Target-Oriented Growth Phase is 1,750,000 TL per year. In 2024, the budget cap was increased to 2,500,000 TL annually.

TÜBİTAK assesses proposals based on university-level parameters such as the university’s maturity, number of faculty members, research budget, etc. Following this evaluation, TÜBİTAK sets annual performance targets for the TTOs. In this new support model, TTOs can organize their activities according to their specific targets.

Description: Tech-InvesTR Venture Capital Support Program was established in order to enable venture capital funds to invest in R&D intensive early-stage companies to meet the financial needs of these companies. In order to ensure sustainable functioning of the program, a Cooperation Agreement was signed between TÜBİTAK and the Ministry of Treasury and Finance.
Objective(s): To address the needs of early stage technology-based start-ups|To foster the commercialization of the results of R&D and innovation|To develop the venture capital ecosystem by incentivizing the creation of new funds.|To provide new incentives tailored to the evolving needs of maturing start-ups.|To increase the number of technology-based start-ups|To raise awareness of technoparks, TTOs and research Infrastructures on venture capital
Background:
The program entered into force with the agreement signed between TÜBİTAK and the Ministry of Treasury and Finance on 14.06.2018. On the same day, TÜBİTAK launched the TechInvesTR-2018 Venture Capital Support Program Call to enable venture capital funds to invest in R&D-intensive early-stage companies, addressing the financial needs of these companies.

The Ministry of Treasury and Finance, Technology Development Zones (TDZs), Technology Transfer Offices (TTOs), and Research Infrastructures (RIs) participate as limited partners (LPs) in independently managed venture capital funds. Additionally, third-party investors, such as commercial banks, investment banks, pension funds, angel investors, private investors, private corporations, public institutions, and foreign institutions like the EIF and EBRD, also participate in the funds as LPs.

TÜBİTAK supports 50% of the contributions made by TTOs, TDZs, and RIs to venture capital funds for investments in early-stage, technology-based companies located in Türkiye, in the form of grants. To ensure the sustainable functioning of the program, a cooperation agreement was signed between TÜBİTAK and the Ministry of Treasury and Finance, under which the Ministry agreed to act as a limited partner.

To sustain the venture capital ecosystem, TÜBİTAK’s grants are tied to capital and experience accumulation conditions in TTOs, TDZs, and RIs. Under the capital accumulation condition, after the fund exits its investments, TÜBİTAK’s share will be reinvested by TTOs, TDZs, and RIs in early-stage, technology-based initiatives. Under the experience accumulation condition, the program aims to transfer the expertise of venture capital management teams to TTOs, TDZs, and RIs. This is expected to enhance the commercialization perspective of these institutions through both experience and capital.

Within the scope of the Tech-InvesTR Program, five venture capital funds have been established. The Ministry of Treasury and Finance signed fund participation protocols with these funds, and project agreements were signed between TDZs, TTOs, and TÜBİTAK for their participation in the established Tech-InvesTR funds.

The Tech-InvesTR funds have reached a total committed size of 5.56 billion TL. This amount is expected to be invested in 150 early-stage, technology-based startups in Türkiye.

As of the end of 2024, the funds have invested in 106 different startups operating in fields such as health technologies, artificial intelligence (machine learning), energy, fintech, online service platforms (marketplaces, payment platforms, wearable technologies, blockchain, logistics operation processes), and mobile game development, with a total investment amount of 2.86 billion TL.

Background: One of the priorities of the National Research Plan 2005-2007, approved in March 2005, was the promotion of the capacities of SMEs to innovate processes and products and form clusters at local and regional level. Description: This initiative is designed to strengthen commercialisation of public research created in univeristies or R&D centres by building competences for managing technology transfer and commercialising R&D.
Objective(s): In order to strengthen the commercialisation of public research, the Transfer and Licensing Offices Programme (Oficinas de Transferencia y Licenciamiento - OTL) seeks to build competences for managing technology transfer and commercialising R&D. Moreover, it seeks to strengthen its IPR framework by improving procedures, protection and enforcement of IPR.
Background: Since its creation in 2011, the initiative has supported 20 institutions (three associatively), which have developed their own models related to transfer and licensing offices. Description: HEIF (Higher Education Innovation Funding) provides funding for HEIs in England to help them maintain and develop their capability to work with business and others through a broad range of interactions with the wider world. It is allocated by Research England. HEIs have flexibility to use HEIF allocations for the full range of Knowledge Exchange activities, and they typically use HEIF to increase their capacity to interact with business (eg though collabroative or contract research and consultancy), enhance their technology transfer activities to commercialise IP (including licensing and IP spin-outs), provide access to facilities and equipment, support for continued professional development; and provide entrepreneurial education for staff and students, and support them starting a business.
Objective(s): Support institutional capacity of HEIs to commercialise research and collaborate and interact with business and other organisations (including third and public sectors).
Background: Higher Education Innovation Funding was established in 2001 in order boost knowledge exchange between Higher Education and the wider world that benefits society and the economy. In 2024-25 funding for HEIF was £280 million. This included a £20million business and commercialisation supplement to drive additional business collaboration and commercialisation performance. Research England have undertaken a comprehensive review of HEIF including an independent long term evaluation 2008-2020 published on 7 February 2025.

Smart specialisation is a new concept in Poland, so there are no specific national or regional programmes or incentives dedicated to it. English name: TÜBİTAK 1702 - Patent-Based Technology Transfer Support Call
Original name(s): TÜBİTAK 1702 - Patent Tabanlı Teknoloji Transferi Destekleme Çağrısı
Description: TÜBİTAK 1702 Support Program promotes the transfer of new patent-based technologies, which emerge as a result of research, development, and innovation projects carried out by higher education institutions, research infrastructures, public research institutions, and early-stage technology companies, to capital companies located in Türkiye through licensing and know-how transfer.
Objective(s): To facilitate the transfer of technologies developed by higher education institutions, research infrastructures, public research institutions, and early-stage technology companies to industry, transforming them into high value-added products, services, and processes.|To enable companies operating in high-technology sectors to benefit from the knowledge and technology produced by higher education institutions, research infrastructures, public research institutions, and early-stage technology companies.|To develop holistic solutions needed by the industry by integrating research, development, and innovation projects carried out by different stakeholders with public resources and emerging technologies.|To ensure the long-term sustainability of technology transfer offices.
Background:
TÜBİTAK 1702 Support Program aims to facilitate the transfer and commercialization of patented technologies developed by higher education institutions, research infrastructures, public enterprises, public research centers and institutes, and early-stage technology companies as a result of scientific R&D and innovation activities. These technologies are transferred to capital companies located in Türkiye through licensing or assignment methods.
TÜBİTAK grants may cover up to 75% of the license or acquisition fee, depending on the scale of the licensee, the technology intensity of the licensed invention, and the geographical coverage of the patents.
The project budget limit is 4 million TRY. Projects submitted to this call must involve one licensee and at least one licensor. The licensee may procure multiple technologies from different licensors within the same project. The base support rate is 25%, with TÜBİTAK providing additional support based on the following conditions:
• +15% if the licensee is an SME,
• +15% if the licensee operates in a high-tech sector,
• +15% if the patent is classified as high-technology based on its International Patent Classification code,
• +15% if the technology transfer falls within the scope of the Green Deal priority domains,
• +10% for patents registered with EPO, USPTO, JPO, CNIPA, or KIPO,
• +10% for projects involving multiple technologies.
The initial call was launched in 2020, followed by two additional calls in 2021 and one in 2022. A total of four calls were issued, and as of 2022, the program has continued as an open call.

Supported projects are monitored each year. At the beginning of each monitoring period, the client deposits contribution into the project account. Then, the support provided by TÜBİTAK to the project is transferred to the project account.

TÜBİTAK grants may cover up to 75% of the license or acquisition fee, depending on the scale of the licensee, the technology intensity of the licensed invention, and the geographical coverage of the patents.
The project budget limit is 4 million TRY. Projects submitted to this call must involve one licensee and at least one licensor. The licensee may procure multiple technologies from different licensors within the same project. The base support rate is 25%, with TÜBİTAK providing additional support based on the following conditions:
• +15% if the licensee is an SME,
• +15% if the licensee operates in a high-tech sector,
• +15% if the patent is classified as high-technology based on its International Patent Classification code,
• +15% if the technology transfer falls within the scope of the Green Deal priority domains,
• +10% for patents registered with EPO, USPTO, JPO, CNIPA, or KIPO,
• +10% for projects involving multiple technologies.
The initial call was launched in 2020, followed by two additional calls in 2021 and one in 2022. A total of four calls were issued, and as of 2022, the program has continued as an open call.

Supported projects are monitored each year. At the beginning of each monitoring period, the client deposits contribution into the project account. Then, the support provided by TÜBİTAK to the project is transferred to the project account.

Objective(s): To increase the number of cybersecurity companies in Türkiye.|To support the development of the technical, administrative and financial capabilities of member companies.|To promote the branding of products and services.|To improve the standards of the cybersecurity ecosystem.|To enhance the competitiveness of member companies in the national and global market.|To increase human capital in the field of cybersecurity & Raise awareness about cybersecurity throughout the society.
Background:
The Turkish Cybersecurity Cluster was established with the aim of developing the cybersecurity ecosystem and serving as a bridge between public institutions, the private sector, and academia.
The planning and coordination of the Turkish Cybersecurity Cluster’s activities are carried out by the Cluster Executive Board, which consists of representatives from the Defense Industry Agency (SSB) and the Digital Transformation Office (DTO). The Turkish Cybersecurity Cluster platform primarily aims to create a Türkiye that produces technology in the field of cybersecurity and competes globally. This aligns with its mission to build a national cybersecurity ecosystem, develop local/national cybersecurity products, and promote their widespread use.
The Turkish Cybersecurity Cluster was formed in 2017 with the participation of all public agencies/organizations, representatives from the private sector and academia, and with the support of the Presidency of Defense Industries. On February 1, 2021, a protocol was signed between the Presidency of Defense Industry (SSB) and the Presidency of Digital Transformation Office (DTO) to jointly execute the activities of the Türkiye Cybersecurity Cluster Platform. The Cluster’s planning and coordination are managed by the Turkish Cybersecurity Cluster Executive Board, while the daily operations of the platform are carried out by the Coordination Office.
The Turkish Cybersecurity Cluster Platform operates under five main pillars: Access to Market, Innovation, Access to Talent, Interaction, and Technological Leadership.
Access to Market: To promote the use and competitiveness of local products in both national and global markets, business development activities, including promotional efforts, are conducted. In addition to promoting their activities domestically and internationally, national companies are encouraged to participate in national and international fairs.
Innovation: To discover new ideas in cybersecurity and promote local products with global competitive power, various entrepreneurship competitions, idea challenges, demo days, and hackathons are organized.
Access to Talent : To nurture the human capital required by Türkiye’s cybersecurity ecosystem and improve the qualifications of the existing workforce, training programs are delivered, camps are organized, and competitions are held periodically. Since 2018, over 3,500 students have been trained through these programs, which continued online during the pandemic. Additionally, to discover new talent, HackIstanbul-Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions and graduation project competitions are organized, and young individuals representing Türkiye abroad are supported.
Interaction: To cultivate the cybersecurity ecosystem and bring together all relevant stakeholders under one roof, national and international conferences, sectoral summits, and SIBERKAFE activities are organized. These events foster interaction both within the sector and with other industries.
Technological Leadership: Various working groups have been established to enable cluster members to collaborate, closely follow technological advancements, and conduct studies in areas required by the sector. The Technology Monitoring Working Group has prepared the Turkish Cybersecurity Cluster product, service, and training catalog. The Export Working Group has conducted studies related to international activities. The Test and Certification Working Group is actively developing test and certification criteria for cybersecurity products, aiming to ensure the reliability of local products through testing and certification.
